Recent investigations into emergent preferences demonstrate that interaction sequences and cultural transmission mechanisms can constrain agent behavior over time. Rather than relying entirely on pre-compiled reward structures, systems exposed to longitudinal environments exhibit consistent patterns of choice and disposition.

Summary: Experience and historical interaction can lead artificial systems to develop stable preferences organically.
